label: 3D, rigging & motion capture
note: The lane most shaped by licence reading: three separate times the best-performing candidate was unusable because a file inside an MIT repo carried a territory clause or a non-commercial training ban.

entities.name: TripoSR
entities.summary: An early image→mesh option, superseded by the 09-19 audit of the whole field.

entities.name: InstantMesh
entities.summary: Replaced in the same audit; no measured defeat recorded, it simply lost the field review.

entities.name: TRELLIS.2
entities.summary: Retired as a generator, but its install is load-bearing for something else: its leftover micromamba prefix is the only nvcc on this box.

issues.text: Its venv imports nvdiffrast at module load, so it is not usable for output on this box.
There is no system CUDA toolkit and no sudo, so every later CUDA build uses TRELLIS.2's conda-forge nvcc 12.4 at ~/TRELLIS.2/cudatk.

entities.name: TripoSG / PartCrafter / DetailGen3D
entities.licence: MIT at repo root, Tencent EU exclusion inside
entities.summary: Removed on a licence read, not a bench: MIT at the repo root, with a Tencent territory exclusion in the core transformer file.

issues.text: The exclusion is inside the core transformer FILE while the repo root says MIT — this is the case that set the rule to read licences at file level.

entities.name: Direct3D-S2
entities.summary: The only candidate in the 09-19 field audit that is MIT in both code and weights and carries no territory clause. Geometry only.

issues.text: EU-clean at file level where the whole Tencent family was not — the reason it won.
Output is geometry only, no texture — the coat has to come from a separate pelage chain.
VRAM scales hard with resolution: sdf_resolution 512 ≈ 10 GB, 1024 ≈ 24 GB.
Needed a hand-built torchsparse against a sparsehash installed into ~/.local, because libsparsehash-dev needs a password this box does not have.

entities.name: Human Generator V4
entities.licence: no AI-training right at any tier
entities.summary: Rejected after the licence was read in full: even the $128 commercial tier grants no AI-training right and no 3D-file distribution.

issues.text: No AI-training right at any tier, including the $128 commercial one, and no 3D-file distribution. Nothing about quality — the licence ends it.

entities.name: MPFB
entities.summary: CC0 human bases in Blender, with CharMorph, MHR, SOMA-X and Z-Anatomy alongside it. CC0 is what makes training and distribution possible at all.

issues.text: CC0 replaced a licence that forbade the two things this stack does with a mesh — train on it and ship it.

entities.name: UniRig
entities.summary: Benched against Blender's bone-heat weights on two meshes and lost on both gate metrics, at both bends. The bench also found two traps that each fake a passing result.

issues.text: Loses to Blender automatic weights on self-intersecting tris AND area-outlier fraction, at both bends on both meshes.

torch 2.6 cannot load its skin checkpoint (weights_only now defaults True and the ckpt pickles a Box) — and generate_skin.sh still exits 0 and prints 'done'. Every future run needs the sitecustomize allowlist shim.
Its merged glb splits every seam vertex, which defeats bone-heat binding AND the self-intersection metric; a stray unit Icosphere is left in every output.

entities.name: Blender automatic (bone-heat) weights
entities.summary: The incumbent that kept its place on measurement. Its failure mode is the dangerous kind: it can silently succeed at nothing.

issues.text: Bone heat silently makes EMPTY vertex groups: all groups get created, parent_set returns FINISHED, only a warning appears — and because the mesh never moves, every deformation metric reads a perfect 0.00. The bench now counts nonzero weights per posed bone.
It is vertex QUALITY, not count: decimating to 14k verts still fails, welding to 166k succeeds, and the weld threshold is per mesh (1e-4 vs 3e-3).

entities.name: GEM-X
entities.summary: Where there was no usable capture path at all: 192 frames in 57 s on 2 GB of VRAM, out to a SOMA BVH and into the CMU rig.

issues.text: Replaced nothing with something — before this there was no usable mocap source, because the SMPL/AMASS route is licence-blocked.

Its SOMA BVH zero-rotation pose is a line along +X, NOT a T-pose, so the converter has to use source frame 0 as the reference skeleton. A proper T-pose frame would need SOMA's t_pose_world applied — not done.
Visual odometry fell back to a static camera (identity camera.pt), so on a moving-camera clip the 'global' translation is camera-relative — the QA subject fought on the spot.
Motion survived the retarget at 8.7% of body height wrist error, and then VACE painted the control plate instead of the boy — the capture was never the weak link.

entities.name: SMPL / AMASS-trained stacks
entities.summary: The standard of the field and unusable here: the SMPL files are non-commercial and unobtainable since Epic bought Meshcapade, and AMASS forbids commercial training.

issues.text: SMPL files non-commercial and no longer obtainable; AMASS forbids commercial training, which taints anything trained on it. The whole own-rig pipeline exists because of this.

entities.name: Procedural lathe anatomy
entities.summary: Three passes of hand-built lathe geometry for anatomy, abandoned in favour of a real CC0 skeleton mesh fitted per segment.

issues.text: Abandoned after three passes — the geometry never read as anatomy.

entities.name: Blender Studio 135-bone skeleton mesh
entities.summary: A real CC0 skeleton MESH fitted per segment to the cmu_mb rig, instead of procedural stand-ins.

issues.text: A-pose toe-out leaked through the delta retarget and the clavicles drove the chest wall — both fixed in the stance/chest pass.

entities.name: SAM 3D Body
entities.summary: Full MHR output from one image — 204 parameters, 70 3D keypoints, per-joint rotations — at 1.2 s/image, with a stable global yaw across a still and a video frame of the same scene.

issues.text: Validated at 1.2 s/image with near-identical global yaw across still and video frame of the same scene.
detectron2 is deliberately absent, so only the single-person branch works.
char_mesh staging and the anny_fit yaw-seed A/B were queued and not done.

entities.name: Blender (bpy)
entities.summary: One of the handful of pre-July tools that survived every swap. It is the scene bridge for Architecture Studio, the rig host, the Cycles renderer for Character Studio and the glTF gateway.

issues.text: Its glTF importer maps the glTF front (+Z) to Blender −Y, so a rule written in the procedural frame must be sign-flipped or it picks the head instead of the tail.
Wall holes in the architecture bridge need real boolean cuts with the EXACT solver, and a cutter must copy the wall's transform or a translated wall keeps its six faces.
